newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania hopes to get credit rating from Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania hopes to get credit rating from Moody's.

text.p: Finance Minister Algimantas Krizinauskas told a news conference on Tuesday Lithuania hoped to get a sovereign credit rating from Moody's in September.
The minister said the rating would reduce Lithuania's borrowing costs on the international market and give the country better access to credit.

Lithuania is set to initial its second syndicated loan in September for $75 million. A senior finance ministry official told Reuters it will be priced at LIBOR + 2.25 percent with a maturity of one year plus one day.
Krizinauskas said 15 banks would participate in the syndicate led by JP Morgan. The loan will be used for general budgeting purposes.
JP Morgan also led the Baltic state's first syndicated loan in April for $33 million. It was priced at 2.5 percent over LIBOR and had a maturity of six months.
